title: How foreign vloggers DEFAME India…
description:
If you watch travel vlogs, you’ve probably noticed a trend. A certain category of foreign vloggers comes to India—not to explore, but to mock. They selectively visit underdeveloped areas, slums, overcrowded trains, unhygienic streets, and then present it as the “real India.”

From calling Delhi the “worst capital” to amplifying obscure village traditions as if the whole country celebrates them, these creators thrive on ragebait. The formula is simple: trigger Indians, get engagement, go viral. Mocking India has become a profitable niche.

Let’s be clear—India has problems. Lack of civic sense, pollution, bad infrastructure. I’ve criticized these issues myself. But there’s a difference between constructive criticism and content designed to fuel racism. Words like “pajeet,” “street shitter,” and “imagine the smell” don’t trend randomly. This ecosystem feeds that narrative.

In this video, we break down how this ragebait economy works, why certain creators keep returning to the same stereotypes, and how our engagement is helping their business model. At the same time, we also highlight foreigners who’ve respectfully documented both sides of India—and even helped create change instead of just farming views.
